name: Constitutional Kernel
known_blockers: PR-1 (organ 25) IMPLEMENTED, status deliberately NOT flipped yet -- see the last two sentences. The gap this organ carried is closed. Measured before the fix (real code, not inference): activating a real amendment moved the durable chain to v2 while EVERY enforcement consumer stayed at v1 forever, because IdentityService._current_constitution_digest, CapabilityAuthority.consume, mirror.py and gateway_reasoning.py each rebuilt a snapshot per call from live config (always version 1), and PolicyKernel.constitution_snapshot() fell through to build_constitution_snapshot(ratified_by_operator_id='operator') in all three real construction sites. The consequence was not cosmetic: consume() compared a rebuilt digest against a binding stamped by the SAME rebuild, so both sides always matched and the 'capability issued under a stale constitution' rejection was structurally unreachable for a real amendment -- its four tests passed only because they compared fabricated literals ('sha256:old-digest') no snapshot ever produced. Separately, aios/api/deps.py referenced ConstitutionAuthority without importing it, so get_constitution_authority() raised NameError -- proof it had never been called. NOW: one ConstitutionAuthority is authoritative for the active snapshot, every Principal's digest, PolicyKernel decisions, capability issuance and consumption, Council context and the mirror projection. The hardcoded 'operator' fallback is deleted (an unwired kernel raises rather than fabricating). Enrollment is re-verified on EVERY call, not only the argument-free one -- the distinction is load-bearing because the two paths that actually run in production both pass an explicit operator id, so a check guarding only the zero-arg path would have guarded nothing; a caller-supplied id is now an assertion to VERIFY, never a chain selector, so an unknown id can no longer mint a second never-amended shadow chain. Fail-closed: NoEnrolledSovereignError / OperatorIdentityChangedError / ConstitutionDegraded, all mapped to one 503 handler. Activation and rollback are compare-and-swap under BEGIN IMMEDIATE with expected_previous_digest REQUIRED (no default), so an unprotected write is a TypeError rather than a silent last-writer-wins; a losing activation raises instead of vanishing. A two-thread race test proves exactly one wins. Also fixed an ordering bug: activate marked the proposal 'activated' BEFORE persisting the snapshot, so a failed write left a proposal claiming an activation that never happened. Verified by tests/test_organ25_constitution_e2e.py, which drives the real HTTP ceremony (ratify consumes a genuine server-issued capability answering the 428 challenge), restarts, then proves the amended digest reaches a fresh Principal and a fresh kernel, that an old-digest capability is refused and a new-digest one succeeds, that rollback survives a restart, and that the mirror reports the amendment. That test is mutation-checked: reverting IdentityService to the per-call rebuild fails all three cases. Deliberately NOT added: a UNIQUE(constitution_id, version) index -- it looks like free belt-and-braces but breaks a sequence this organ's own contract requires (after a rollback to v1, activating a new amendment under any changed config yields a different v2 digest at the same version). REMAINING before green, and the only reason this row is still yellow: green-contract conditions 11 and 12 -- the exact tested commit must be recorded here and verified by a CI run on that same commit. Full local backend suite is exit 0; CI on the pushed branch has not yet run.

name: Communication and Human-State Interpreter
known_blockers: PR1 (organ 30 closure, fixing the exact bug named for this pass): migration 0013 stored a correction by MUTATING corrected_state/corrected_at columns directly on the original hypothesis row, while the row's own record_digest kept authenticating only the ORIGINAL hypothesis fields -- corrections were silently overwriteable (a second correction just overwrote the first, with no history) and sat outside the tamper check entirely (the digest never covered corrected_state/corrected_at, so tampering them left the digest valid). Migration 0014 replaces this with a genuinely append-only, digest-verified human_state_corrections table (one row per correction event, never mutated), joined to its hypothesis by row id (hypothesis_id) rather than content digest -- a content-digest join was tried first and rejected: two hypotheses with identical content on different turns produce the SAME digest, which silently collapsed two distinct corrections into one accuracy-report bucket (caught by a new regression test before it shipped). Each correction row is bound to the authenticated operator via get_optional_principal() -- recording None honestly when no principal is bound, never a fabricated identity -- and accuracy_report() now aggregates only the newest valid correction per hypothesis. A live tamper-detection regression test directly mutates the new table and confirms RecordTamperedError is raised, closing exactly the gap the operator named. Stays yellow: the deterministic classifier itself still has not been measured against real production operator traffic -- the corrections table (now genuinely tamper-evident) is exactly the mechanism that will let that happen as real traffic accumulates, but no such traffic exists yet in this sandbox; a genuine, not-fabricatable gap, not a wiring gap.

name: Installation, Configuration and Key Authority
known_blockers: Key rotation and a bounded grace period are now real (operator-confirmed design: grace-period overlap, not an immediate hard cutover). New ApiTokenAuthority (aios/application/security/api_token_authority.py) issues a fresh API bearer token via a new POST /api/v1/security/api-token/rotate route; the token it supersedes keeps working for a caller-chosen grace period (default 3600s) so an already-running client is not broken the instant rotation happens, then stops validating once the window elapses -- proven with a fake-clock unit test, not just asserted. config.API_TOKEN (the env-configured value) stays unconditionally valid exactly as before this organ existed -- the operator retires it the normal way, by restarting with a different env var; this authority only owns tokens issued through an explicit rotate() call, layered on top, so every pre-existing test and behavior around the static token is unchanged. A real regression was caught and fixed before shipping: an early draft cached config.API_TOKEN's value inside the long-lived authority singleton at first construction, so a test elsewhere in the suite that temporarily reassigns config.API_TOKEN would permanently poison every later, unrelated test in the same process -- caught by real adversarial-suite regressions (tests/adversarial/test_api_security.py), not by a test written for this change; fixed by making the authority stateless with respect to config.API_TOKEN (every method takes it fresh as an argument) rather than caching it. Still missing: 'truthful Ollama-absence handling' -- the other named half of this organ's original blocker -- has no further specification anywhere in the repo beyond that one paraphrased sentence, and is an unrelated concern (local-model availability reporting, not credential rotation); not investigated or built in this pass.
